items.q: This page treats membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis and mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis as names for the same entity.
opts: True — the eponym line reads 'a.k.a. mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis' for MPGN
False — mesangiocapillary GN is the older term for IgA nephropathy
False — the two are separated by which complement pathway is involved
True — and the page notes that the entity is common in children
items.exp: a.k.a mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis; rare disease. (Book p770)

items.q: Match each MPGN column with its feature — 1) Type I immunofluorescence (capillary wall & mesangium) 2) Type II immunofluorescence 3) Type II outcome post transplant … A) 100% recurrence B) C3 ± IgG/M C) IgG + IgM ± C3
items.exp: Type I IF: IgG + IgM ± C3; Type II (C3 GN): C3 ± IgG/M; Type II post transplant: 100% recurrence. (Book p770)

items.q: C3 glomerulonephritis is the label this page attaches to type II MPGN.
opts: True — type II is labelled C3 GN
False — C3 GN is the label written against type I MPGN
False — the page prints C4 GN beside type II MPGN
True — and the same label is applied to post-infectious GN

items.q: Outcome post transplant in the classification table: Type I recurs in 80% of cases while Type II recurs in:
items.exp: Type I 80% recurrence; Type II 100% recurrence. (Book p770)

items.q: A resident wants to know whether a search for systemic causes can be skipped in a biopsy-proven MPGN. The banner over the secondary-cause block of the table states:
opts: All (100%), as the banner of that block reads
Only the type I subset, which is about half of cases
None — MPGN is always treated as a primary disease
A fifth of cases, and only when an infection is found
items.exp: Secondary causes (100% cases are secondary to systemic causes). (Book p770)

items.q: The monoclonal (malignancies) row of MPGN secondary causes lists plasma cell dyscrasias and:
opts: Chronic lymphoid leukemia (CLL)
Hodgkin lymphoma with Reed-Sternberg cells
Acute myeloid leukemia with circulating blasts
Multiple myeloma as the only listed entity
items.exp: Monoclonal: plasma cell dyscrasias; chronic lymphoid leukemia (CLL). (Book p770)

items.q: A child returns from a malarious region with nephritic features and low C3; the infection line of the type I table is read. Which organisms and diseases appear on that line?
opts: Hepatitis C, infective endocarditis, leprosy and P. malariae
Plasmodium falciparum with cerebral involvement, not quartan malaria
Hepatitis B with schistosomiasis, the pair seen in membranous disease
HIV and parvovirus B19, the pair listed under secondary FSGS
items.exp: Infections: HCV, infective endocarditis, leprosy, Plasmodium malariae (Quartan malarial nephropathy). (Book p770)

items.q: The shunt example and autoimmune trio under polyclonal Type I causes are:
opts: Ventriculoperitoneal shunt; SLE, Sjogren's, scleroderma
Atrial shunt; SLE, RA, Sjogren's
Ventriculoperitoneal shunt; SLE, RA, scleroderma
Portosystemic shunt; Sjogren's, scleroderma, RA
items.exp: Shunts: eg. ventriculoperitoneal shunt; autoimmune: SLE, Sjogren's, scleroderma. (Book p770)

items.q: Type II MPGN's polyclonal associations are acquired partial lipodystrophy of face and:
opts: Optic nerve drusen
Retinitis pigmentosa
Optic neuritis
Papilledema
items.exp: Type II: acquired partial lipodystrophy of face; optic nerve drusen. (Book p770)

items.q: Match each deposit feature with its MPGN type — 1) Type I EM appearance 2) Type I deposit location 3) Type II deposit location … A) Intramembranous + mesangial B) Train track/double contour appearance C) Subendothelial + mesangial
items.exp: Type I: train track/double contour; subendothelial + mesangial. Type II: intramembranous + mesangial. (Book p770)

items.q: Type II MPGN carries the eponym intramembranous dense deposit disease.
opts: True — intramembranous dense deposit disease is the eponym
False — dense deposit disease is the eponym reserved for type I MPGN
False — the eponym printed for type II is type III MPGN
True — and both labels imply that complement studies are normal
items.exp: AKA intramembranous dense deposit disease. (Book p770)
